title: Agent skill authoring — Claude override
description: What Anthropic's own 'Skill authoring best practices' (Claude Platform Docs) adds to the shared base voice agent-skill-authoring: Claude's front-matter validation, its naming conventions, forward-slash paths, and three authoring methods (plan-validate-execute, no voodoo constants, author with one instance and test with another). MODEL-SPECIFIC by the owner's ruling (bean rkqp): a vendor's advice is evidence about that vendor's platform. Provenance ASSERTION: a publisher describing its own product. Rules the base already carries — much of it traceable to this very document (the ~500-line body, one-level references, a table of contents over ~100 lines, third-person descriptions, evaluations before instructions) — are inherited through extends, not repeated. Conformance is an agentic review, never a schema gate.

sources.title: Skill authoring best practices | Claude Platform Docs (captured 2026-09-20)

rules.title: name ≤ 64 characters of lowercase, digits and hyphens; description ≤ 1,024 characters; no XML tags in either
rules.description: Claude validates the SKILL.md front matter: name at most 64 characters, lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens only, no XML tags and no reserved words; description non-empty, at most 1,024 characters, no XML tags. A skill that breaks these does not load on Claude, which is why this is a vendor rule — other platforms state different limits or none.

source.quote: The SKILL.md frontmatter requires name and description fields with specific validation rules: name : Maximum 64 characters, lowercase letters/numbers/hyphens only, no XML tags, no reserved words description : Maximum 1,024 characters, non-empty, no XML tags

rules.title: Prefer a gerund name — processing-pdfs, not pdf-helper
rules.description: Anthropic's preferred form is the gerund (processing-pdfs, analyzing-spreadsheets); noun phrases (pdf-processing) and action-oriented names (process-pdfs) are acceptable alternatives. Pick one pattern for a whole collection: inconsistency within a collection is listed among the things to avoid.

source.quote: Remember that the name field must use lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only. Good naming examples (gerund form): processing-pdfs analyzing-spreadsheets managing-databases testing-code writing-documentation Acceptable alternatives: Noun phrases: pdf-processing , spreadsheet-analysis Action-oriented: process-pdfs , analyze-spreadsheets

rules.title: No vague, generic or reserved names
rules.description: helper, utils and tools say nothing; documents, data and files are too generic to route on; names containing the reserved words (anthropic-helper, claude-tools) are refused.

source.quote: Avoid: Vague names: helper , utils , tools Overly generic: documents , data , files Reserved words: anthropic-helper , claude-tools Inconsistent patterns within your skill collection

terminology.context: a name that states the work, not a category

rules.title: Forward slashes in every file path, even on Windows
rules.description: scripts/helper.py, never scripts\helper.py: Unix-style paths work on every platform, Windows-style ones fail on Unix systems.

source.quote: Always use forward slashes in file paths, even on Windows: ✓ Good: scripts/helper.py , reference/guide.md ✗ Avoid: scripts\helper.py , reference\guide.md Unix-style paths work across all platforms, while Windows-style paths cause errors on Unix systems.

rules.title: Every configuration value in a bundled script says why it is that value
rules.description: A magic number in a script is a value Claude cannot reason about: if the author does not know why it is right, the model cannot determine it either. Justify and document each constant (Ousterhout's 'voodoo constants').

source.quote: Configuration parameters should also be justified and documented to avoid "voodoo constants" (Ousterhout's law). If you don't know the right value, how will Claude determine it?

rules.title: For a complex, open-ended change: plan in a structured form, validate the plan with a script, then execute
rules.description: The intermediate plan is the checkable artefact — mistakes (a non-existent field, a conflicting value, a missed requirement) are caught before anything is changed, not after.

source.quote: When Claude performs complex, open-ended tasks, it can make mistakes. The "plan-validate- execute" pattern catches errors early by having Claude first create a plan in a structured format, then validate that plan with a script before executing it.

rules.title: One term per concept, throughout the skill
rules.description: Choose a term — 'API endpoint', 'field', 'extract' — and never alternate it with a synonym inside one skill; a variant reads to the model as a different thing.

source.quote: Use consistent terminology Choose one term and use it throughout the Skill: Good - Consistent: Always "API endpoint" Always "field" Always "extract"

rules.title: Write the skill with one Claude instance and test it with another
rules.description: Anthropic's authoring loop: 'Claude A' helps design and refine the instructions; 'Claude B', a separate instance with the skill loaded, uses it on real tasks and exposes what is missing. Begin by doing the task once without a skill and noting the context you kept supplying — that is the skill's content.

source.quote: Claude ("Claude A") to create a Skill that is used by other instances ("Claude B"). Claude A helps you design and refine instructions, while Claude B tests them in real tasks.
